prompts:
Use case: illustration-story. Production sprite atlas, transparent background. Input1 is the SIX EXISTING KEY POSES of a cute Korean magpie looking at a butterfly. Input2 is the original character standing/walking reference, first bird is canonical resting pose. Create IN-BETWEEN drawings that will be inserted between the existing Input1 poses. Preserve this exact charcoal silhouette character, tiny white circular eye, rounded belly with thin dark contour, white shoulder, LONG tail rising diagonally right, feet planted, same body scale.
Output exactly SIX whole-bird drawings in 3 columns x 2 rows, evenly spaced with full-tail padding. Read left to right, then next row:
0 TOP LEFT: exact canonical resting bird from Input2 first frame, head looking horizontally LEFT. This is registration reference.
1 TOP MIDDLE: halfway between Input1 frames0 and1, head/beak raised only 12.5 degrees above LEFT horizontal.
2 TOP RIGHT: halfway between Input1 frames1 and2, head/beak raised 40 degrees above LEFT horizontal.
3 BOTTOM LEFT: halfway between Input1 frames2 and3, head/beak raised 72.5 degrees above LEFT horizontal, almost up but still slightly left.
4 BOTTOM MIDDLE: halfway between Input1 frames3 and4, head/beak leaning 17.5 degrees RIGHT of vertical, a near-up head transitioning to upper-right.
5 BOTTOM RIGHT: halfway between Input1 frames4 and5, head/beak pointing upper RIGHT 40 degrees above horizontal.
DO NOT repeat the original key angles25/55/85. The five intermediate angles are12.5/40/72.5 left,72.5/40 right. Head and neck articulations must be natural complete drawings; no floating pieces. Keep torso, white shoulder patch, belly outline, long up-right tail, and feet at identical local positions across all cells. Do not make new character. Do not enlarge/shrink heads or bodies. Do not mirror body for right gaze. Preserve the existing plumpness and thin outline. Charcoal #2e2a26 and white, flat crisp shape. No butterfly, scenery, baseline, shadow, glow, labels, text. Actual transparent background.

Edit this sprite sheet. Preserve all SIX DIFFERENT head directions exactly. Do not turn the birds all to the left. Only shorten the neck of the bottom-left bird slightly, lowering that same tilted-up head by about20 pixels. Also shorten the neck of the bottom-middle bird slightly, lowering that same upper-right tilted head by about12 pixels. All heads keep their current angle and size. Keep every other detail exactly unchanged: torso, feet positions, tail, wing markings, belly, transparent background, sheet dimensions. No other edits.
discarded: Two alternative attempts rejected because head directions did not fit the required intermediate sequence; not copied into project.
